metadata.title: GUILD, the growth agent that only pays for verified results
metadata.description: Give GUILD a target and a budget. It recruits partners, verifies the results they bring, and pays the real ones in USDC on Arc inside limits it cannot change.

a.text: Built for the Tameion Agents Hackathon on Arc
The growth agent that only pays for results it can verify.

GUILD recruits partners, sets each one’s incentive inside your cost ceiling, verifies every outcome they bring, holds the suspicious ones, and pays the rest in USDC on Arc within hours. Your budget, your ceiling and your approval limit are enforced by a contract the agent cannot change.
Built for the Tameion Agents Hackathon by Canteen, Circle and Arc. Open source. The first campaign is live now.
Three steps, one message
You read a log, not a dashboard. Every payout, hold and decline has its reasons attached and its transaction linked.

a.$control__text1: Developers who activate on Acme. 200 USDC. Up to 8 per activation.
a.$control__text2: Paid signups on Lumen. 500 USDC. No more than 12 per purchase.
a.$control__text3: Wallets that complete one swap on Arc. 150 USDC. Up to 5 each.

a.text: Example mandate
Fund campaign
Set the mandate

Tell GUILD what outcome you want, how much you will spend in total, and the most you will pay per result. Add the line that defines a real result: a purchase, an activation, an onchain action your product can vouch for. GUILD turns that into a campaign and funds it onchain. The budget and the ceiling are now limits it cannot cross.
Partners bring results

GUILD opens an apply link, reads each application, accepts the ones that fit, and offers each partner an incentive under your ceiling. Partners get a referral link and a wallet. When someone they brought does the real thing, your product’s backend tells GUILD, signed.
GUILD deciding
GUILD verifies and pays

Every result is attributed, scored for fraud, and held through a cooling window. The ones that check out are paid in USDC on Arc within hours, once, to the partner’s locked address. The ones that do not are held with the evidence, and you only hear about it when a policy line is crossed.
The decisions it makes so you do not have to
The agent proposes and explains. Deterministic code decides. The contract enforces. That order never changes.
Who to work with
Reads every application, accepts the partners whose plan and history fit, and says why it declined the rest.
@devrel_sam: Solana devs group, 1.2k
@maya: weekly newsletter, accepted at 6 USDC
@kai: declined, no stated channel
Screening: clear
What to offer
Sets each partner’s incentive under your ceiling, pays more to partners whose results keep verifying, and counters bids that ask for more.
Where the budget goes
Moves remaining budget toward the partners who deliver, pauses the ones who stop, and slows down if the money would run out before the deadline.
At this rate the budget runs out Saturday 21:00, before the Sunday 09:00 deadline. New events move to the 5 USDC tier. Say hold the tier to keep 6.
Budget: 42 spent, 6 held, 152 remaining of 200. Cost per verified activation 6.0 USDC against your 8 ceiling.
When to ask you
Only above your approval limit, when a partner’s fraud rate spikes, or when a partner changes their payout address. Two buttons in your chat; everything else is a log entry.
What counts, what is real, when to pay.

A payout exists only because the product emitted a signed qualifying event, the referral mapped to an accepted partner, the fraud score stayed under the line, the cooling window passed, and the amount fit inside the limits.
What counts
Accepts a result only when your product vouched for it, signed, and the referral matches a partner it actually accepted.
When to pay
Waits out the cooling window, voids anything reversed, then pays once to the partner’s locked address.
What is real
Scores every result for self-referral, bursts, duplicates and timing, lists the signals, and holds anything over the line.
The order never changes
The model vets and explains, and never holds a key.
Bring real users. Get paid in hours, not months.

You know people who should be using a product. GUILD pays you in USDC for every one of them who does the real thing, within hours of it being verified, at a rate you agreed to up front. No minimum payout, no monthly cycle, no processor taking a cut, and you can be paid on Arc or on the chain you already use.

a.$control__title: Apply with a few lines. GUILD answers inside the hour.
Accept the incentive or counter once. Get a link and a wallet.
Share the link. Results show pending, cooling, then paid.
Paid results land in your wallet with a transaction link.

a.text: Tracking tools track. GUILD decides.
Keep your tracking tool if you like it. GUILD is the thing that was missing on top of it: the part that decides.

a.$control__description: Affiliate software applies the commission you configured to everyone. GUILD takes your ceiling, sets each partner’s incentive, and changes it as results come in.
There, a referral is payable because a pixel fired. Here, a result is payable because your product vouched for it, signed, and the fraud score stayed under the line.

a.$control__industryName: Fraud is a hold, not a report
a.$control__description: There, fraud is a report you read at the end of the month. Here, it is a hold with the signals attached, before any money moves.

a.$control__industryName: Paid in hours, for about a cent
a.$control__description: There, payouts run on a schedule, through a processor, with a fee. Here, they settle in USDC on Arc within hours of cooling, for about a cent, to a locked address.

a.$control__industryName: Budget is a cap in a contract
a.$control__description: There, budget is a number in a settings page. Here, it is a cap in a contract the agent cannot raise.

a.$control__industryName: A log a reviewer can replay
a.$control__description: There, you get a dashboard. Here, you get a decision log a reviewer can replay, with every payout linked to its record.

a.text: Free during Tameion. Honest after it.

You fund your own budget; GUILD takes no fee from it. Payouts on Arc cost about a cent each, paid from the campaign. You own the campaign, the partner relationships and the records. Export them any time.
Limits the agent cannot talk its way past
Budget cap
The campaign cannot pay out more than you funded. The agent cannot raise it.
Per-result ceiling
No single payout exceeds the number you set. Partners bid below it; the agent never bids above it.
Pay once, after cooling
Every result has an id; the contract refuses to pay it twice. Nothing pays before the cooling window ends.
Locked payee
Partners are paid to the address they onboarded with; a change freezes payouts until you approve. Anything above your limit waits for your two-button answer.
A receipt proves money moved. The record proves why.

Every decision writes a record: the event, who it was attributed to, the signals scored, the cooling clock, the budget before and after, the policy line, and the transaction. Its hash is stored with the payment. Partner addresses are screened against the OpenSanctions crypto-wallet list at application and before every payout. Below, the record format in the words the bot uses.

$control__testimonials.role: Record hash stored with the payment

$control__testimonials.name: Hold record
$control__testimonials.role: Partner stays active, voided if reversed in cooling

$control__testimonials.name: Escalation
$control__testimonials.role: Two buttons in your chat

$control__testimonials.quote: New partner application: @maya. Shares in the Solana devs group (1.2k) and a weekly newsletter. Screening clear. Accept at 6 USDC per activation.
$control__testimonials.name: Partner decision
$control__testimonials.role: Accepted in 10 min unless you say otherwise

$control__testimonials.quote: At this rate the budget runs out Saturday 21:00, before the Sunday 09:00 deadline. New events moved to the 5 USDC tier.
$control__testimonials.name: Pacing notice
$control__testimonials.role: Say hold the tier to keep 6

$control__testimonials.quote: Screening hit on 0x3c…9e against the OpenSanctions crypto-wallet list. Partner blocked. No agent decision can override this.
